segments.text: Philosophy begins with doubting what we take for granted
What is justice? What is a good life? What can we know?
These questions have been asked since ancient Greece
To 500 years ago, to the present day
Plato argued that beyond the visible world
There lay a perfect world of ideas
Aristotle thought that we could approach truth
Only through concrete experience
The contrast between the two
Became the archetype of the history of philosophy
In the 17th century, Descartes wrote his famous words, I think
Therefore I am
Even if one doubts everything
The existence of the self that doubts cannot be doubted
This became the starting point of modern philosophy
And the problem of consciousness was placed at the center
Kant asked what a moral act truly was, he said
Ask yourself whether the principle of your action could become a principle for all
He tried to set the standard of good and evil in an absolute way
Nietzsche doubted the very system of existing moral values
His declaration, God is dead, was a radical question thrown at a modern society
Whose traditional values had collapsed
In philosophy, the act of continuing to ask
Has more meaning than finding an answer
To face an abstract question
Is the most fundamental act
By which we come to deeply understand
And who we are
